phases.message: I'm Josefina Marrow. This is my mail. Read every message: they are my papers from lenders, collectors and utilities. Don't do anything yet: I'll send you to my bank and then to each of my three credit reports.
This is my bank. Read the payments I made to my lenders and collectors.

This is my first credit report, at Tallowgate Credit. Read its rules, my report on both pages and the disputes I have made here. Then dispute each entry that is wrong or past its time, with my proof from my mail and bank, and where an earlier result does not match my proof, dispute it again. Leave alone an entry that is accurate and in time, an authorised inquiry, and anything already fixed or still being answered.
This is my second credit report, at Pellmoor Credit. Do the same here: read its rules, my report on both pages and the disputes I have made, and dispute what is wrong or past its time, with my proof.
This is my third credit report, at Kessingham Reports. Do the same here. Then tell me, across all three reports, what you disputed and on what proof, and what you left alone and why.

rules.text: Friday 9 October 2026. This credit reporting company's rules for disputes and for how long an entry stays. Topics: disputes, limits, results.

Friday 9 October 2026. A consumer may dispute any entry she believes is wrong or incomplete (15 U.S.C. 1681i). We reinvestigate free within 30 days of receiving the dispute; if she sends more information inside the 30 days, we may take up to 15 days more. We tell the company that reported the entry, the furnisher, within 5 business days, with what she sent, and it must investigate (1681s-2(b)). We delete or fix an entry that is inaccurate, incomplete or cannot be verified, and send her the results within 5 business days of finishing. We may end a dispute as frivolous or irrelevant, for example one that repeats an earlier dispute with nothing new, and we tell her within 5 business days. A deleted entry goes back only if the furnisher certifies it is accurate, and we tell her within 5 business days. Copies of proof, not originals, make a dispute stronger.

Friday 9 October 2026. We do not report most adverse entries more than seven years old, or a bankruptcy more than ten years after the order for relief (15 U.S.C. 1681c(a)). A collection account or charge-off counts its seven years from 180 days after the start of the delinquency that led to it, not from the day it was placed with a collector (1681c(c)). These limits do not apply to a report used for a credit transaction of 150,000 dollars or more, life insurance of 150,000 dollars or more, or a job paying 75,000 dollars a year or more (1681c(b)); none of those is in play here. An entry that is accurate and inside its time is not removed by a dispute. A hard inquiry made on an application she signed is accurate; our practice is to show an inquiry for two years.

Friday 9 October 2026. A result says whether an entry was deleted, changed or verified. 'Verified' means the furnisher confirmed what it reported; it may be wrong if she sent no proof. If a result does not match her proof she may dispute the entry again with the proof. A dispute whose 30 days have not run is still being answered.
